proposals: MoSPI should publish a combined CPI reading for every state in each monthly release on api.mospi.gov.in, or state in the release which states are omitted and why, so the 15 grey states on a map like this one are no longer indistinguishable from states with low inflation.

MoSPI should publish state-level CPI by commodity group in the same API dataset as the state headline, so a pattern like June 2026's southern clustering — Telangana at 6.36%, Andhra Pradesh at 5.39% — can be traced to food or other items without a separate item-level release.

The Office of the Economic Adviser in DPIIT should publish a note on whether a state-level WPI breakdown is feasible from the price quotations it already collects, since WPI currently has no state-level series and only CPI can be mapped this way.

The RBI should include a table of state-wise CPI against the 2–6% tolerance band in each Monetary Policy Report, so the gap between the national rate policy responds to and the rates individual states are living with, such as Telangana above the band in June 2026, is officially on record.
